content:
Based on 9to5Mac's website traffic analysis, Apple is testing iOS 27.0.1 for iPhone. This update will most likely focus on bug fixes and performance improvements.

iOS 27.0.1 is coming soon

Analysis data from 9to5Mac began showing signs of iOS 27.0.1 a few days ago. MacRumors also has related reports.

Apple told 9to5Mac this morning that it will release a software update early next week to address an issue where some iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models unexpectedly restart after a failed Face ID authentication.

We previously reported on this issue, explaining that when you try to use Face ID to unlock apps like "Passwords" and others, if Face ID authentication fails, your iPhone may unexpectedly reboot.

I was never able to reproduce this issue on my own iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, but it has clearly affected quite a few users. The good news is that this is a bug that can be fixed with a software update, not any kind of hardware fault.

It's very likely, though unconfirmed, that iOS 27.0.1 will address that issue. It may also include other bug fixes affecting iOS 27 and the new iPhone 18 Pro hardware.

Since updating to iOS 27, have you encountered any issues? How about issues specific to the iPhone 18 Pro? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
